item.title: Can Governments Enforce Their Way Out of the Illicit Market Crisis? | #GFN Voices 2026 #4
item.description: Enforcement cannot fix a market that policy itself is helping to create. Illicit nicotine trade grows where demand remains high, legal access is restricted and safer products are pushed outside accountable channels. Police action may disrupt supply, but it cannot remove the incentives that make illegal sales profitable. A serious response to the illicit market crisis has to combine enforcement with harm reduction, realistic regulation and legal options that adults will actually use. (Published on August 19, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: What do AI assistants tell users about tobacco harm reduction?
item.description: AI assistants are becoming part of how people look for health advice, including advice on smoking and vaping. That makes the quality of their answers more than a technical issue: it can shape whether smokers understand relative risk, switching and the dangers of continued combustion. Vague or overly cautious responses may feel safe, but they can leave people with a distorted view of lower-risk alternatives. Digital health information should be accurate, proportionate and clear enough to support real-world harm reduction. (Published on August 20, 2026bymoregoodlessharm.com)
